sections.html:
Up in the northeast corner of DeSoto County, Olive Branch sits against the Tennessee line as part of the Memphis metro area. Its 39,711 residents in 2020 made it the sixth most populous city in Mississippi. Memphis city limits touch part of the northern border, Southaven lies to the west, and unincorporated DeSoto County wraps the east and south. U.S. 78, Highway 302 (Goodman Road) and Highway 305 (Germantown Road and Cockrum Street) all pass through, and downtown Memphis is about 22 miles northwest on U.S. 78.

The city covers about 36.9 square miles. A 1996 annexation to the west doubled the land area, and the growth after it means most of the city is newer subdivisions rather than old downtown blocks. A small historic core remains around Olive Branch Old Towne, so a house there may be older and sit on a different lot pattern than the big subdivisions.

Its housing numbers are lopsided. Homeowner vacancy was 1.0 percent in 2020 and rental vacancy 16.1 percent, with 6.1 percent of the 15,542 housing units vacant across 14,599 households. Landlords with a vacant rental may wait months to fill it, and some weigh a cash sale against renovating and finding a new tenant.

Olive Branch began as Watson's Crossroad and was incorporated in 1873. Only about 200 people lived there at the turn of the twentieth century, and water service did not arrive until 1922 or electricity until 1927. The 1990 census counted 3,567 residents, and by 2000 the number was 21,054. Houses near Olive Branch Old Towne, which has a historic trail, shops, festivals and murals, can therefore be much older than the subdivision homes that fill the rest of the city. Older construction often means older wiring, plumbing and roofs, which a buyer's inspector will test.

Warehousing and distribution anchor the local economy, and the city counts on that industrial base for tax dollars that fund schools, the library and infrastructure. For a seller the point is simple: land near you can change use as projects move ahead. Before you list, find out what is planned near your address, because buyers will ask and the answer can move the price either way.

Permits come through Planning and Development. Its Building Department issues them for all construction and inspects the finished work. The Code of Ordinances has a chapter on buildings and building regulations, posted on Municode. Code enforcement is reachable at 662-892-9342.

Without city approval, outdoor sales and storage are off limits. Any accessory building used for storage needs its own building permit. If an earlier owner put up a shed, carport or garage without one, resolve it before you sell. The city enforces ordinances meant to protect public health, safety and quality of life, so if you sell a house you do not live in, ask whether a complaint is open against it.

sections.h2: How DeSoto County bills property tax
sections.html:
State law puts the due date at February 1 after the January 1 assessment, and DeSoto County issues the bill. The tax collector keeps offices in Hernando, Olive Branch and Horn Lake and answers at 662-469-8030. You can search tax receipts online.

Because the house is inside city limits, its bill combines a county rate, a school district rate and a city rate. Assessors count an owner-occupied home at 10 percent of true value, and the county must reassess real property at least once every four years.

DeSoto County's tax sale is held on the last Monday in August, and a delinquent parcel that draws no buyer passes to the State. Settle back taxes before closing so the title stays clean. Recording fees at the chancery clerk are set by statute, and the county has a fee calculator on its land records page.

The state's exemption comes in three tiers. File at the Tax Assessor's office in Hernando; for 2027, DeSoto County's window is January 4 to April 1. The exemption can shift with a buyer's circumstances, so expect a new owner to reapply.

sections.h2: Listing, selling alone or taking cash
sections.html:
Choices here are an agent listing, a sale by owner or a cash buyer. A well-kept house can do well on the open market. Cash tends to win out if the house needs work, a tenant lives in it, or the move date is close. Buyers who finance will order an appraisal and an inspection, so deferred maintenance can slow a conventional sale.

Before title transfers, the seller owes the buyer a written property condition disclosure statement. One that shows up after an offer lets the buyer cancel, within three days if handed over in person or five if mailed. Do the form carefully.

Our offers are for the house as is, with no commission and no closing costs charged to you. Send us an Olive Branch address and we will explain how the offer is built. The decision stays with you.

Any sale follows one order. Terms are agreed, a title search finds liens or unpaid taxes, balances come out of your proceeds, and the deed is signed at closing, then recorded by the chancery clerk. Come with photo ID, a payoff figure for any mortgage, tax receipts, and permit papers covering sheds, garages or additions.

What a cash sale skips is the buyer's lender. No appraisal ordering, no loan approval and no repair demands from an inspection report means fewer places for the date to slip. What it does not skip is your own cleanup: back taxes, open complaints and unpermitted structures still need to be dealt with, or priced into the offer.

sections.h2: Getting the house ready for a buyer's questions
sections.html: Think about what a buyer or investor in Olive Branch is likely to ask: how old the roof and wiring are, whether the shed or garage was permitted, whether the lot is in a newer subdivision or near the older core, and what is going up nearby. Write short answers ahead of time. If you own a rental, add the lease terms and how long the unit has been empty. Clear, honest answers keep a deal from stalling, and they protect you if a question comes back after closing.

Investors frequently buy houses with tenants in place. Start by pulling the lease, then speak with an attorney about the tenant's rights before settling on a closing date. Give the buyer the lease and rent records, and tell the tenant what to expect. A vacant rental that has sat through a long tenant search costs you taxes, insurance and utilities each month, which is a good reason to price a sale against the cost of waiting.

faqs.q: Is Olive Branch, MS part of Memphis?
faqs.a: No. Olive Branch is a city in DeSoto County, Mississippi, on the Tennessee state line. It is part of the Memphis metro area, and the center of Memphis is about 22 miles away by U.S. 78.

faqs.q: When are DeSoto County property taxes due, and when is the tax sale?
faqs.a: Payment is due February 1 for the January 1 assessment, at any of three collector offices in the county. The tax sale takes place the last Monday in August, and a parcel nobody buys goes to the State.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a shed in Olive Branch?
faqs.a: Yes, if the shed is used for storage. Call the Building Department before you build, and again before you sell if the shed went up without one.

faqs.q: What is the homestead filing window in DeSoto County?
faqs.a: The county's window is January 4 through April 1, 2027, handled at the Tax Assessor's office in Hernando. State law allows applications from January 1 to April 1.

faqs.q: Must I give a disclosure statement when selling in Mississippi?
faqs.a: Usually yes, under Section 89-1-503, and it has to arrive before title transfers. If it comes late, the buyer may cancel within three days of in-person delivery or five days of mailing.
